Subject: ScapeBio pilot — purchase routing & PO approval timeline

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a single place to track: 

Summary of what we heard
- Pilot scope: 10k tokens/day, LLM generation + embeddings for a 6-week proof-of-concept.
- Primary constraint: SCAPE procurement prefers a formal PO route for vendor onboarding; AP needs a supplier packet and W9 before payment.
- Time sensitivity: engineering wants to start data ingestion within 2 weeks if we can get a procurement path.

Questions / clarifications needed from SCAPE
- Preferred commercial path: do you want to proceed via a PO (standard enterprise) or do you have flexibility for a card-based pilot to speed things up?
- Marketplace interest: would AWS Marketplace (or Azure Marketplace) be acceptable to accelerate onboarding?
- Vendor packet: AP asked what specific docs Redwood can provide up front (W9, remittance address, supplier form, insurance cert).
- Invoice terms preference: Net-30 / Net-45 / Consolidated monthly invoice?

Attachments I can share now
- vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf (attached) — basic packet we typically send to AP teams
- redwood-draft-sow.docx — short SOW template if you want to attach to a PO

Proposed next steps
1) If PO required: Oliver, please confirm who in procurement will own the PO and an estimated approval lead time so we can set a go/no-go date.
2) If Marketplace acceptable: we can route pilot through AWS Marketplace to shorten procurement; I can share a one-pager and link.
3) If you prefer a quick card test: we can provision a limited-card charge with an invoice later (requires AP sign-off on card limits).

Happy to jump on a 15-min call with SCAPE AP and our finance team to walk through the packet and timeline. What works best?

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot moving.

—

Thanks for the clear recap, Jasmine — this is helpful. A few notes from procurement/AP side: 

- Our default is PO for any vendor engagement that might run beyond a nominal pilot. For a pilot at this scale we still typically require a PO because of internal spend controls.
- AP requires a completed supplier form + W9 + remit address + tax ID before they can issue a PO. Once they have that, legal will do a brief review (we expect ~2–4 weeks for approvals).
- Marketplace: we will discuss internally whether AWS Marketplace could be used for the pilot to speed things up — that would be ideal because it often bypasses parts of our supplier onboarding. However, marketplace procurement also has its nuances (billing flow, seat/usage lines, and different contracts).
- Invoice terms: our default is Net-30, but we can be flexible for pilots. Consolidated monthly invoicing is preferred by our AP team.

I will loop in our AP contact (ap@scapebio.com) to start the supplier packet. If you can send the completed packet and the marketplace link, I can escalate this afternoon.

Oliver Reed
Director, Procurement Operations
SCAPE Bio

Adding some commercial/finance options that have worked for customers in this exact spot: 

Options to move fast
1) Temporary card route (fastest): allow a one-time corporate card charge or capped card payment for the pilot (we typically cap at the expected pilot spend + 20%). Good when engineering needs to start in <2 weeks. AP needs to approve the single-card exception for amounts >$25k.
2) Marketplace (fast + auditable): Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace. Marketplace onboarding can be ~3–7 business days from our side (customer side sometimes quicker). This usually reduces the supplier packet friction but changes billing flow to AWS. No immediate change to product or SLA.
3) Standard PO (enterprise-preferred): provide completed supplier packet + W9 + draft SOW and wait for PO issuance (2–4 weeks typical). Works for long-term engagements.

Implications / pricing
- If you want to do a short-term card pilot, we can offer the pilot at standard list with an option to credit unused committed spend back if you choose to convert to a PO and annual commit.
- Marketplace purchases sometimes preclude certain discounting mechanics, so we may need to align on commercial terms up front.

Attachments I recommend we send to SCAPE AP now: vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf (includes remit address, W9, certs) and redwood-draft-sow.docx (short SOW language we can attach to a PO).

Recommended next step: propose a 15-min triage with SCAPE AP this week to choose path (Marketplace vs PO vs card). If SCAPE wants to push through PO, we should confirm the procurement owner and expected approval window so we can coordinate engineering start dates.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Oliver — quick note from finance side: 

- Our AP team can accept either PO or card for a pilot. Practical constraints: any single charge above $25k typically requires Procurement sign-off for a card exception.
- If SCAPE wants Net-30 consolidated invoicing on a monthly cadence, we can do that under a standard PO.
- If time is the blocker, we routinely suggest the following hybrid: start on Marketplace or a capped card for the first 2–4 weeks (so engineering can begin) then convert to a PO for the remainder. We will provide a credit or true-up if pricing differs when converted.

If SCAPE agrees, we can set up a 15-min call between SCAPE AP, Jasmine, and our finance ops (looping Neha) to formalize any card exception or to confirm marketplace routing. Let me know a couple of time windows and I will get finance on the calendar.

Thanks —
